newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends down on technical adjustment.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends down on technical adjustment.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed lower, extending their downtrend on technical adjustment coupled with lack of fresh leads, dealers said.
"There was still some adjustment in prices following the ringgit's strength against the U.S. dollar," said one local dealer.
Trading remained sluggish in the absence of fresh buying interest, dealers said, adding that closure of the Tokyo market for a holiday further limited activity.
They added that buyers have met most of their rubber requirements for the first quarter of 1997.
"Far East consumers have sufficient stocks and are unlikely to buy in the near future," another dealer said.
He said ample supply of raw materials, due to a recent turnaround in the weather, was putting pressure on prices.

At the close, February RSS1 buyer was quoted at 304 cents ($1.23) a kg by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board, down one cent from Tuesday. February SMR 20 buyer was also down a cent at 300.50 cents ($1.21) a kg.
Traders offered the SMR 20 at 301 cents, SMR CV at 369, SMR L at 350, SMR5 at 317, SMR 10 at 302 and drum latex FOB at 236.
